games.2026_03_ATL_GB: Two teams whose ratings collapsed in Week 2 meet on a short week. Green Bay is losing Jayden Reed and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele to IR on top of Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs, with Aaron Banks doubtful and Javon Hargrave still in concussion protocol. Atlanta is worse: a 34-3 home loss dropped its rating nearly four points, A.J. Terrell and Samson Ebukam are doubtful, and Michael Penix Jr. makes his first start since the ACL tear at Lambeau with four days of preparation. The model has the Packers by seven; the market says six.
games.2026_03_CAR_CLE: Carolina's rating jumped after the 34-3 win in Atlanta, but the Panthers still play without both starting tackles, Nic Scourton and Tershawn Wharton, and Jonathon Brooks is doubtful. Cleveland won in Tampa with Deshaun Watson, though the Browns rate as one of the worst teams in the league and have Teven Jenkins doubtful and Tyson Campbell questionable. On the data alone this is a pick; the market has Carolina by 2.5, and the blend makes the Panthers a coin-flip road favorite.
games.2026_03_CIN_PIT: Cincinnati is 2-0 and its rating has risen almost three points on two solid, low-drama wins; Burrow played through back tightness in Houston and reported no setbacks. Pittsburgh managed 188 yards in New England and has Rico Dowdle, Troy Fautanu, Michael Pittman and Joey Porter Jr. all questionable. Model and market agree on Bengals by three to three and a half in a divisional game with a narrower distribution.
games.2026_03_HOU_IND: A divisional game between two 0-2 teams and the largest model-versus-market disagreement of the week. Houston's rating has fallen four and a half points on two poor games and the injury list keeps growing: Nico Collins is out again with a hamstring, Ed Ingram is out, Clowney is questionable, and three linebackers are gone. Indianapolis gave up 41 and 33 and is without Alec Pierce for several weeks. On the data alone the Colts are 2.5-point home favorites; the market moved to Houston by three. The blend is a pure coin flip, with Houston the pick by the thinnest margin.
games.2026_03_KC_MIA: Kansas City's rating climbed again after the overtime win in Indianapolis and Mahomes looks fully back, but left tackle Josh Simmons and safety Chamarri Conner remain out. Miami is a bottom-three team by rating, 0-2 with a first-year starter at quarterback, Kenneth Grant on IR and Chop Robinson questionable. Heat and a 50 percent storm chance at Hard Rock compress the margin slightly. The model has the Chiefs by eight; the market's 11.5 is richer than the data supports, so the blend is under ten and Kansas City is a High pick rather than Very High.
games.2026_03_LAC_BUF: Buffalo is 2-0, rated fourth in the league, and comes off a Thursday game with ten days of rest, worth a modest rest edge. The Chargers are 0-2, rated below average after two losses, and lost both tight ends (Njoku and Kolar) to IR this week plus guard Kayode Awosika and Dalvin Tomlinson, on top of Biadasz and Perryman. DJ Moore and Ed Oliver are questionable for Buffalo. The model has the Bills by more than 13; the market's seven pulls the blend to under ten, and this is the model's biggest edge on a favorite.
games.2026_03_NE_JAX: Jacksonville had its nine-game win streak snapped in Denver but remains a top-six team by rating and is nearly at full strength. New England shut out Pittsburgh's offense but is missing A.J. Brown, Harold Landry and now right guard Mike Onwenu (broken ankle), and Drake Maye has thrown four interceptions to one touchdown. The model has the Jaguars by four at home; the market says three.
games.2026_03_NYJ_DET: Detroit's rating dipped after allowing 41 in Buffalo, and safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph remain on PUP with Mahogany and Miller questionable on the line, but the Lions get ten days of rest and a dome. The Jets are the second-lowest-rated team on the slate: Minkah Fitzpatrick and Omar Cooper Jr. are still doubtful, David Onyemata is out, and Mason Taylor is questionable. The model has the Lions by nearly ten; the market by 6.5.
games.2026_03_SEA_WAS: Seattle is the top-rated team in the model and 2-0 with Drew Lock; Sam Darnold returned to practice Wednesday in some capacity and Macdonald says his timetable has shifted drastically, so the model gives him roughly a 40 percent chance to start. Washington lost Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow and turns to Marcus Mariota, with Laremy Tunsil, Johnny Newton and Trey Amos still on IR and Sam Cosmi in concussion protocol. The model has the Seahawks by nearly 14 on the road; the market's seven pulls the blend to ten, and Seattle is the strongest pick of the week.
games.2026_03_TEN_NYG: Both teams are 0-2 and rated in the bottom quarter. The Giants' situation got worse Tuesday: Jaxson Dart's MRI was worse than feared and he could miss the rest of the season, so Jameis Winston (11 of 27 in relief Monday) is the starter, and Malik Nabers (shoulder), Brian Burns (ankle) and Andrew Thomas (groin) are all questionable on a short week. Tennessee blew a late lead to Philadelphia but is relatively healthy. The market shortened to Giants by 2.5; the model has them by one at home, and the blend is about two, a Lean.
games.2026_03_ARI_SF: San Francisco is 2-0 and rated third, but its receiver room is gutted: Demarcus Robinson joins Ricky Pearsall and Christian Kirk on IR, and Mike Evans is questionable with a hip. Arizona lost Will Johnson for possibly the season with a neck injury, is without Garrett Williams and James Conner, and was routed by Seattle. Divisional game, narrower distribution. The model has the 49ers by more than ten; the market's 8.5 brings the blend to about nine.
games.2026_03_MIN_TB: Minnesota is 2-0 with a defense that allowed three points in Chicago, and Kyler Murray returns from concussion protocol, which the model counts as the biggest quarterback boost on the slate over what the Vikings fielded last year. Tampa Bay is 0-2, rated below average, and has Jacob Parrish questionable, but the roster is otherwise intact. Heat in Tampa. The model has the Vikings by nearly five on the road; the market has 1.5, and the blend is three.
games.2026_03_BAL_DAL: The second neutral-site game abroad this season, at the Maracanã in Rio, with Dallas the designated home team and no home-field edge for either side; the model widens the variance for the travel and the rain-worn pitch. Baltimore's rating is still fourth despite the loss to New Orleans, but Zay Flowers, Ronnie Stanley, Trey Hendrickson and John Simpson all sat out Wednesday's practice and Madubuike was limited; Minter says several have a good shot. Dallas is the healthier side at quarterback but its secondary is depleted: P.J. Locke and Cobie Durant are out for weeks, Hooker and Overshown are doubtful, and Tyler Smith is on IR. The model has the Ravens by six; the market moved to 3.5.
games.2026_03_LV_NO: New Orleans beat Baltimore and gets Alvin Kamara and Cameron Jordan back, but lost left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. to IR with a high-ankle sprain and has Martin Emerson questionable. Las Vegas is 2-0 with Kirk Cousins, rated better than its preseason number, and expects Brock Bowers back. Both quarterbacks grade as upgrades on what their teams fielded last year. Superdome, so no weather. Model and market both have the Saints by about three.
games.2026_03_LA_DEN: The Rams rate second in the league after the Monday-night win over the Giants, with Aaron Donald back, but Myles Garrett is on IR and Puka Nacua is questionable after being scratched Monday; Los Angeles also plays on six days of rest against Denver's seven. The Broncos beat Jacksonville but rate near average, with both running backs (Dobbins and Harvey) questionable and Marvin Mims doubtful. Altitude and a Sunday-night crowd give Denver a strong home edge. The model has the Rams by nearly four; the market says 1.5, and the blend is two and a half.
games.2026_03_PHI_CHI: Chicago's quarterback room has collapsed in 48 hours: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is unlikely to play, Tyson Bagent entered concussion protocol Tuesday, and if he is not cleared by Monday, 38-year-old Case Keenum starts his first game since 2023. The model treats it as a deep-backup start with wide variance, a four-and-a-half-point downgrade, with Kyler Gordon still on PUP. Philadelphia is 2-0 but its rating has fallen after two narrow wins, and the Eagles lost Dallas Goedert for several weeks on top of Landon Dickerson, with Jonathan Greenard still questionable. The market moved from Eagles by three to 4.5; on the data alone the Bears are slight home favorites, and the blend makes Philadelphia a Lean.
